message: The client was a cold-chain logistics operator delivering food and pharmaceuticals. Revenue grew but margins fell. The interviewer wanted us to explain the falling margins and recommend how to restore profitability over the next year. The cause was a mix shift into sparse pharma routes. Fewer deliveries per trip raised cost per kilo but prices were still based on dense food routes, so the growth reduced margins. Local competitors undercut prices on dense routes. Two wrong paths were blaming fuel inflation without checking route density, and exiting pharma rather than repricing sparse routes. The insight was that route density, not revenue, determines unit economics. This was a Bain interview in August 2026.
